name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The generalist Bachelor of Business at Kaplan is the base version of a degree the school also sells with five bolt-on majors, so it's worth understanding what's actually compulsory before deciding whether the plain version or one of the named variants makes more sense. Only six subjects across the whole three-year degree are core: five foundational units at Level 100 covering business communication, accounting, economics, commercial law and numerical skills, plus a single Level 200 subject on governance, ethics and sustainability. Everything else, all the way through Level 300, is elective, which means this version of the degree is genuinely a choose-your-own-adventure business qualification rather than a management or marketing degree with a different label stapled on.

That structure suits two kinds of students: those who want breadth across accounting, marketing, management and IT without committing to a named major, and those transferring in in with credit from a Diploma of Business or another provider who want to fill out electives around whatever they've already completed. Nine trimesters and 24 subjects gets a full-time student through in three years, with intakes running five times a year (March, May, July, September, November) rather than the usual two-semester cycle, which is a real practical advantage for students who don't want to wait out a gap year to start.

Level 300 also carries the degree's two internship subjects, which give students who haven't locked in a specific career direction the chance to test an industry placement without it being tied to one major. It's an AQF Level 7 qualification, CRICOS-registered, and available at all five KBS campuses (Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney), though the named-major versions of the degree aren't offered everywhere.
curriculum:
Level 100 core: Business Communication (BUS101); Introduction to Accounting (BUS103); Economics (BUS104); Commercial Law (BUS107); Skills for Numerical Analysis (BUS109)
Level 200 core: Governance, Ethics and Sustainability (MAN202)
Level 300: no compulsory core subjects — students select electives across accounting, marketing, management, hospitality and IT streams, including Internship 1 (BUS307) and Internship 2 (BUS308)
Structure: 24 subjects across 9 trimesters, full-time, 3 years; five intakes per year
Delivery: Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney

name: Bachelor of Business (Accounting)
description:
This is the accounting-major version of KBS's Bachelor of Business, and the accounting content only really kicks in once the shared foundation year is out of the way. The first five subjects (business communication, intro accounting, economics, commercial law, numerical analysis) are identical to every other Bachelor of Business student at KBS, and the single Level 200 core (governance, ethics and sustainability) is also shared. What makes this a genuine accounting degree rather than a business degree with an accounting flavour is the block of electives students are steered toward at Level 200 and 300: financial accounting, management accounting, taxation law, auditing, and corporate law units that map onto what CPA Australia and CA ANZ expect to see for graduates seeking a pathway into the CPA Program or CA ANZ's professional entry route.

Students who complete this major and want to go further don't have to leave KBS to do it: the school's Master of Accounting picks up where this degree leaves off and carries its own accreditation from CPA Australia, CA ANZ and ACCA, so a student can plan a five-year run from school leaver to professionally accredited accountant without changing institutions. That continuity matters more here than in some of the school's other majors, since accounting is one of the few fields where the professional body's unit-mapping requirements genuinely shape what gets taught rather than the university choosing freely.

Like the rest of the Bachelor of Business suite, the degree runs on trimesters (nine trimesters, 24 subjects, three years full-time) with five intakes a year, and the two Level 300 internship subjects give accounting-track students a chance to sit inside a firm before graduating rather than only after.
curriculum:
Level 100 core (shared foundation): Business Communication (BUS101); Introduction to Accounting (BUS103); Economics (BUS104); Commercial Law (BUS107); Skills for Numerical Analysis (BUS109)
Level 200 core: Governance, Ethics and Sustainability (MAN202)
Accounting major electives (Level 200-300): Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Taxation Law; Auditing and Assurance; Business and Corporations Law; Financial Reporting
Level 300 options: Internship 1 (BUS307); Internship 2 (BUS308)
Structure: 24 subjects across 9 trimesters, full-time, 3 years
Delivery: Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney (accounting major availability varies by campus — confirm current intake)

name: Bachelor of Business (Hospitality and Tourism Management)
description:
This is the outlier in the KBS Bachelor of Business family: instead of accounting, marketing or management electives layered onto the generalist core, students stack hospitality and tourism operations subjects, covering areas like hospitality service management, tourism destination planning, event management and hospitality law. It sits under subject area codes distinct from the rest of the business suite for a reason: tourism and hospitality in Australia is a genuinely separate industry with its own regulatory and seasonal quirks (visa-dependent international student labour, tourism board relationships, hotel and events sector cyclicality) that a generic business degree doesn't really touch.

The shared foundation is identical to every other Bachelor of Business student at KBS: communication, accounting, economics, commercial law and numerical analysis in Level 100, governance/ethics/sustainability at Level 200. Where this major earns its name is in the Level 200-300 stream, which brings in operations-focused units aimed at hotel, resort, tourism board, airline and events employers rather than the corporate management track. The two internship subjects at Level 300 do a lot of work here, since hospitality and tourism hiring in Australia still runs heavily on demonstrated on-the-job experience, and a KBS internship placement in this major is more likely to land in a hotel, resort or tourism operator than a corporate office.

Graduates commonly move into hotel and resort management, event coordination, tourism marketing or destination management roles, and the degree's international student intake (KBS runs large cohorts from source markets like India, Nepal and China) means classroom discussion of hospitality service standards tends to draw on a genuinely global range of hospitality norms rather than an Australia-only frame.
curriculum:
Level 100 core (shared foundation): Business Communication (BUS101); Introduction to Accounting (BUS103); Economics (BUS104); Commercial Law (BUS107); Skills for Numerical Analysis (BUS109)
Level 200 core: Governance, Ethics and Sustainability (MAN202)
Hospitality and Tourism Management major electives: Hospitality Service Management; Tourism Destination Planning; Event Management; Hospitality Law and Risk; Rooms Division and Resort Operations; Tourism Marketing
Level 300 options: Internship 1 (BUS307); Internship 2 (BUS308) — commonly placed with hotel, resort or tourism operators
Structure: 24 subjects across 9 trimesters, full-time, 3 years
Delivery: check current campus availability; historically concentrated at Sydney and Melbourne

name: Bachelor of Business (Management)
description:
The management major is the most conventional read of KBS's Bachelor of Business: it takes the shared foundation (business communication, accounting, economics, commercial law, numerical analysis, then governance/ethics/sustainability) and layers on the Level 300 subjects the school specifically flags as its advanced management core: dynamic strategy, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, management in global business, and managing change. That's a more deliberately generalist manager-track than the accounting or marketing majors, aimed at students who want to move into supervisory and management roles across any industry rather than a functional specialism.

One practical caveat: KBS notes that its Management and Marketing programs aren't currently available at the Brisbane and Perth campuses, so this major is realistically an Adelaide, Melbourne or Sydney option at present. The Level 300 subjects reappear as MBA elective options too (dynamic strategy and entrepreneurship in particular), so a student who does this major as an undergraduate and later returns for an MBA at KBS will recognise some of the same subject titles at a more advanced level, which is either a nice continuity or a reason to look elsewhere for genuinely new content, depending on how you view it.

As with the rest of the suite, it's 24 subjects across nine trimesters, full-time three years, with the two Level 300 internship subjects available to build workplace experience before graduating, useful for a major where a management job title tends to require some demonstrated track record even at graduate level.
curriculum:
Level 100 core (shared foundation): Business Communication (BUS101); Introduction to Accounting (BUS103); Economics (BUS104); Commercial Law (BUS107); Skills for Numerical Analysis (BUS109)
Level 200 core: Governance, Ethics and Sustainability (MAN202)
Level 300 management core: Dynamic Strategy; Entrepreneurship; Creativity and Innovation; Management in Global Business; Managing Change
Level 300 options: Internship 1 (BUS307); Internship 2 (BUS308)
Structure: 24 subjects across 9 trimesters, full-time, 3 years
Delivery: Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney (not currently offered at Brisbane or Perth campuses)

name: Bachelor of Business (Marketing)
description:
Marketing at KBS sits on top of the same generalist foundation as every Bachelor of Business student (communication, accounting, economics, commercial law, numerical analysis in the first year, one ethics and governance subject in the second), and then diverges through a run of Level 200 and 300 electives built around consumer behaviour, digital and social media marketing, brand strategy and marketing analytics. The degree isn't marketed with a heavy digital-first pitch the way some newer marketing degrees are; it reads more as a traditional marketing major that has folded digital channels and analytics in as electives rather than rebuilding the whole degree around them, which suits students who want a broad marketing grounding rather than a narrowly digital one.

One practical note for anyone comparing campuses: KBS states plainly that its Marketing (and Management) programs aren't currently offered at the Brisbane and Perth campuses, so students set on this major need to check availability at Adelaide, Melbourne or Sydney before enrolling. The two Level 300 internship subjects are open to marketing-track students and are one of the more direct ways to turn the degree into agency or in-house marketing experience before graduation, given how heavily entry-level marketing hiring in Australia still leans on demonstrated placement or agency exposure.

As with the rest of the Bachelor of Business family, it's a 24-subject, nine-trimester degree with five intake points a year, which in practice means a student starting in a November intake finishes roughly three years later without waiting on the standard February/July university calendar.
curriculum:
Level 100 core (shared foundation): Business Communication (BUS101); Introduction to Accounting (BUS103); Economics (BUS104); Commercial Law (BUS107); Skills for Numerical Analysis (BUS109)
Level 200 core: Governance, Ethics and Sustainability (MAN202)
Marketing major electives (Level 200-300): Consumer Behaviour; Marketing Communications; Digital and Social Media Marketing; Brand Management; Marketing Analytics; Services Marketing
Level 300 options: Internship 1 (BUS307); Internship 2 (BUS308)
Structure: 24 subjects across 9 trimesters, full-time, 3 years
Delivery: Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney (not currently offered at Brisbane or Perth campuses)

name: Graduate Diploma of Business Administration
description:
The Graduate Diploma of Business Administration is best understood as roughly the front half of the KBS MBA, packaged as a standalone exit point. Students who want postgraduate business credentials but aren't ready to commit to the full 12-subject MBA, whether for cost, time, or visa-related reasons, take a subset of the same core leadership, governance and financial literacy units plus a smaller elective load, and finish with a qualification that's also directly stackable: KBS structures the Grad Diploma so that credit carries across into the MBA if a student later decides to continue.

In practice this credential does two jobs for two different kinds of students. It's an exit award for people partway through the MBA who need to leave study early with something to show for it, and it's also a deliberate entry point for students whose undergraduate degree or work background doesn't quite clear the bar for direct MBA admission, giving them a shorter, lower-stakes program to demonstrate postgraduate-level capability before stepping up. Either way, it shares the trimester structure and multi-campus footprint of the rest of the KBS postgraduate suite.

Because it's shorter than the MBA, there's less room for elective specialisation, so the degree leans on the shared core (leadership and people management, governance and ethics, and financial/economic literacy for managers) rather than offering the eight-track specialisation menu the full MBA carries.
curriculum:
Core subjects: People, Culture and Contemporary Leadership (MBA401); Governance, Ethics and Sustainability (MBA402); Financial and Economic Interpretation and Communication (MBA403)
Electives (selected from the MBA elective pool): typically drawn from Consumer Behaviour and Marketing Psychology, Dynamic Strategy, International Business, Project Management
Structure: 8 subjects, shorter than the full 12-subject MBA; credit pathway into the MBA for students who continue
Delivery: Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney, or online

name: Master of Accounting
description:
KBS built the Master of Accounting with triple accreditation in mind: CPA Australia, Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, and ACCA all recognise it, which for an international student cohort matters more than it might for domestic-only accounting programs, since it gives graduates a credential that's portable if they end up practising outside Australia. At 16 subjects across six trimesters (two years full-time), it's a heavier load than the school's other master's degrees, reflecting how much technical ground a professionally accredited accounting qualification has to cover: financial and management accounting, financial reporting, auditing and assurance, corporations law, taxation law, and a dedicated accounting information systems unit.

What's distinctive is how far the elective list leans into analytics rather than traditional accounting electives: students choosing from strategic management accounting, data visualisation, data acquisition and management, AI and machine learning, and business analytics project management, alongside a more conventional internship option. That reflects a broader shift in how accounting firms hire: the analytics-minded electives are clearly there to produce graduates who can sit inside a Big Four or mid-tier firm's advisory or analytics practice, not just its audit or tax compliance teams.

The capstone, Accounting and Governance, closes the degree by pulling the technical subjects together into governance and reporting judgement calls rather than pure technical computation. It's the kind of synthesis a CPA or CA ANZ pathway expects graduates to demonstrate before they're considered ready for the professional program's practical experience requirements.
curriculum:
Core subjects (13): Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Advanced Financial Accounting; Financial Reporting; Auditing and Assurance; Information Systems in Accounting; Business and Corporations Law; Taxation Law; Economics; Finance; Analytics in Accounting and Finance; Quantitative Methods; Capstone: Accounting and Governance
Electives (choose 3): Strategic Management Accounting; Introduction to Business Analytics; Data Visualisation and Communication; Data Acquisition and Management; Data Security and Ethics; Data-driven Forecasting; Marketing and Social Media Analytics; Business Analytics Project Management; Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning; Innovation and Creativity in Business Analytics; Internship
Accreditation: CPA Australia, Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ), ACCA
Structure: 16 subjects across 6 trimesters, full-time, 2 years
Delivery: Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Sydney, Perth

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Kaplan Business School runs its MBA on a trimester clock rather than the semester rhythm most Australian universities use, so a full-time student can finish 12 subjects in two years across six trimesters spread over campuses in Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney, plus an online cohort for anyone juggling the degree around a job. The six core subjects lean toward the interpersonal and interpretive side of management: leadership, governance and ethics, financial and economic literacy for non-finance managers, consumer psychology, and a cross-cultural intelligence unit that reflects how much of the cohort tends to be international postgraduates working alongside local managers already in industry.

What separates it from a generic MBA is the elective architecture. Rather than a single fixed specialisation, students pick six electives (or condense that to three plus a three-subject specialisation block) from a list that spans dynamic strategy, entrepreneurship, international business, digital marketing, project management, healthcare and tourism management, and an internship placement. KBS picked up a PIEoneer award in 2020 for its approach to flexible content delivery, and the specialisation model is really an extension of that: eight named specialisation tracks, from Data-driven Leadership to Women in Leadership, let two people graduate with the same base MBA and quite different transcripts.

The degree closes with a capstone strategy subject that asks students to work a live business problem end to end, drawing on the core units rather than treating strategy as an abstract elective. For students who already hold significant industry experience, Recognition of Prior Learning can shorten the path, which matters for a program whose average student profile skews toward people returning to study mid-career rather than straight out of an undergraduate degree.
curriculum:
Core subjects: People, Culture and Contemporary Leadership (MBA401); Governance, Ethics and Sustainability (MBA402); Financial and Economic Interpretation and Communication (MBA403); Consumer Behaviour and Marketing Psychology (MBA404); Emotional Intelligence, Cultural Intelligence and Diversity (MBA502); MBA Capstone: Strategy (MBA600)
Electives (choose six, or three plus a three-subject specialisation): Dynamic Strategy, Entrepreneurship, International Business, Digital Marketing, Project Management, Tourism and Hospitality Management, Healthcare Management, Analytics electives, Internship
Optional specialisation tracks (replace three electives): Data-driven Leadership, Project Management, Health Services Management, Tourism and Hospitality Leadership, Digital Management, Entrepreneurship, International Leadership, Women in Leadership
Structure: 12 subjects across 6 trimesters, full-time, 2 years standard pace; part-time and accelerated options available
Delivery: Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney campuses, or fully online
admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor Degree (or AQF Level 7 equivalent) in any discipline; alternatively, an Advanced Diploma or Associate Degree (AQF Level 6 equivalent) plus a minimum of two years' relevant industry experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0, with not less than 6.0 in Speaking and Writing and 5.5 in Listening and Reading (KBS's published Bachelor/Postgraduate English entry requirement).

name: Master of Business Analytics (Information Technology)
description:
The Information Technology stream of KBS's Master of Business Analytics builds on the same core analytics subjects as the standard degree (data acquisition, visualisation, security and ethics, forecasting, AI and machine learning, quantitative methods) but points the elective and specialisation choices toward IT infrastructure and systems concerns rather than purely commercial analytics applications. At five trimesters (one year eight months) full-time, it's noticeably shorter than KBS's Master of Accounting, reflecting the more compact, technically-focused nature of the analytics field compared with a professionally accredited accounting qualification.

The degree closes with an Analytics Capstone built around an industry research project, which in the IT-focused variant tends to mean students working through a genuine data or systems problem sourced from an organisation rather than a synthetic classroom case, and it's positioned by the school as substantial preparation for further postgraduate study as much as direct employment, since KBS notes it carries credit into related postgraduate IT and analytics courses elsewhere.

Graduates from this stream typically move into business analyst, data/reporting analyst or business intelligence roles, sitting at the intersection of the commercial decision-making side of analytics (forecasting, marketing analytics, project management) and the more technical AI/machine learning and data security content. It's a combination that suits students who want to work with data teams without retraining as software engineers or data scientists from scratch.
curriculum:
Core subjects (9): Introduction to Business Analytics; Data Visualisation and Communication; Data Acquisition and Management; Data Security and Ethics; Data-driven Forecasting; Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning; Analytics in Accounting and Finance; Quantitative Methods; Analytics Capstone: Industry Research Project
Electives (choose 3, IT-focused): Artificial Intelligence Programming in Business Analytics; Business Analytics Project Management; Marketing and Social Media Analytics; Innovation and Creativity in Business Analytics; Internship
Structure: 12 subjects across 5 trimesters, full-time, 1 year 8 months
Delivery: Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney

name: MBA (Health Services Management)
description:
This is the health services specialisation running inside KBS's standard MBA chassis: same six core subjects on leadership, governance, financial literacy, consumer behaviour and cultural intelligence, capped off with the same strategy capstone, but three of the elective slots are swapped for a dedicated health services management block. That's a meaningful distinction from a standalone Master of Health Administration: students here graduate with an MBA, not a health-specific credential, which suits people aiming for general management roles inside hospitals, aged care providers or health insurers rather than clinical or health-policy careers specifically.

The specialisation content covers managing healthcare teams, service delivery models and the operational and workforce pressures particular to the sector: rostering clinical staff, navigating funding models tied to Medicare and private health insurance, and the compliance load that comes with operating in a heavily regulated industry. Given how much of Australia's health workforce is trained overseas and re-credentialed locally, and how many KBS postgraduate students are themselves international, the cohort composition for this specialisation tends to include a real mix of people already working clinically who want a move into management, alongside career changers from unrelated industries.

It runs on the same trimester calendar as the base MBA (12 subjects, six trimesters, two years full-time), with the option to compress or extend the pace, and is offered across the same national campus network plus online delivery.
curriculum:
Core subjects (shared with base MBA): People, Culture and Contemporary Leadership (MBA401); Governance, Ethics and Sustainability (MBA402); Financial and Economic Interpretation and Communication (MBA403); Consumer Behaviour and Marketing Psychology (MBA404); Emotional Intelligence, Cultural Intelligence and Diversity (MBA502); MBA Capstone: Strategy (MBA600)
Health Services Management specialisation electives (three subjects): Healthcare Systems and Policy; Managing Health Services Teams; Health Service Operations and Funding
Remaining electives: chosen from the general MBA elective list (Dynamic Strategy, International Business, Digital Marketing, Project Management, Internship, etc.)
Structure: 12 subjects across 6 trimesters, full-time, 2 years standard pace
Delivery: Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney, or online

name: MBA (Project Management)
description:
Project Management is one of the eight specialisation tracks layered onto KBS's standard MBA structure, and it's aimed squarely at students who want PM methodology and credentials attached to a general management degree rather than a narrower Master of Project Management. The six core MBA subjects (leadership, governance, financial literacy, consumer behaviour, cultural intelligence, and the strategy capstone) stay the same; what changes is three of the elective slots, replaced with subjects covering the full project lifecycle: initiation and scoping, risk analysis, team leadership under project constraints, and evaluating project outcomes against original business cases.

KBS pitches the specialisation as "industry-informed," and in practice that shows up in the electives sitting alongside genuinely commercial content rather than an academic treatment of PMBOK theory alone. Students in this track often pair the project subjects with electives in digital marketing or business analytics to build toward specific industries (construction, IT delivery, health infrastructure) rather than treating project management as a discipline in isolation. That flexibility is really the point of doing this as an MBA specialisation instead of a dedicated postgraduate PM degree: graduates come out with the broader people-management and strategy grounding of an MBA, with project delivery skills as the differentiator on top.

Same trimester structure as the base MBA: 12 subjects, six trimesters, two years full-time, available across the national KBS campus network and online, with Recognition of Prior Learning available for students who've already managed projects professionally and can demonstrate it against specific subjects.
curriculum:
Core subjects (shared with base MBA): People, Culture and Contemporary Leadership (MBA401); Governance, Ethics and Sustainability (MBA402); Financial and Economic Interpretation and Communication (MBA403); Consumer Behaviour and Marketing Psychology (MBA404); Emotional Intelligence, Cultural Intelligence and Diversity (MBA502); MBA Capstone: Strategy (MBA600)
Project Management specialisation electives (three subjects): Project Initiation and Scoping; Project Risk Analysis; Leading Project Teams
Remaining electives: chosen from the general MBA elective list (Dynamic Strategy, Digital Marketing, Business Analytics, International Business, Internship)
Structure: 12 subjects across 6 trimesters, full-time, 2 years standard pace
Delivery: Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney, or online
